Alex: Quick sync — we need a concrete acceptance pact for console observability: dashboards, tracing hooks, cost breakdowns, error analytics. Customer asks piling up. Can we lock wireframes + SLOs by EOD Friday?
Maria: Do we mean hard SLOs or acceptance criteria for launch?
Alex: Acceptance criteria that product can sign off on (not final SLOs). Think: required widgets, minimal trace span tags, cost breakdown slice, and error analytics MVP queries.
Priyanka: Proposed split: Must-have (dashboards + cost by model route, basic traces with span-level errors) vs Nice-to-have (per-tenant sampling controls, advanced correlation views).
Sam: From infra: tracing hooks require a small schema change (span.tag: model_version, route_id). We can land that in 2 sprints if prioritized.
Jen: FYI engineering capacity — two full weeks for dashboards (backend + metrics + UX), one week for cost breakdown prototype. Tracing hooks parallel but needs trace tag rollout plan.
Maria: If customers want canary tracing, we need rollout policy in docs. Is that in scope for the pact?
Priyanka: Not for MVP. Include rollout playbook as a non-blocking deliverable for Beta. MVP acceptance: docs describing rollback & sampling defaults.
Sam: infra-bot: Created ticket RDW-2314 with trace schema proposal: https://go/redwood/tickets/RDW-2314 :ticket:
infra-bot: Note: Estimated infra effort: 8 dev-days across 2 engineers.
Alex: OK — let's commit to the following minimal acceptance checklist. Jen/Maria, confirm feasibility?
```
ACCEPTANCE CHECKLIST (console observability MVP)
- Dashboards: 3 tiles (overall request rate, 95p latency by route, error rate by model)
- Cost breakdown: cost by model + cost by route for last 7d + peak-cost alert
- Tracing hooks: span.tag model_version + route_id + error_flag present in 90% of sampled spans
- Error analytics: error-class buckets + top 5 stack traces for uncaught errors
- Docs: rollout/playbook, sampling defaults, rollback steps
- UX: wireframe + basic interactions (time range, route filter)
```
Jen: Feasible but two caveats: 1) the 90% span tagging is optimistic for older model infra; we can guarantee 70% initially and a plan to 90% in sprint+1. 2) Top 5 stack traces requires retention adjustments for traces (adds cost).
Maria: Agree on lowering initial guarantee to 70% and adding a metric to track tagging coverage.
Priyanka: So updated pact: target 70% tagging in MVP, with documented plan & metric to reach 90% within 30 days post-launch.
Alex: Approved. Final question: can QA produce a small prompt set to validate quality regressions tied to cost changes? Might be product + research.
Sam: Research/QA collaboration OK. I'll add RDW-2315 for eval harness.
infra-bot: Created ticket RDW-2315: eval harness for cost/quality checks.
Jen: Action items: Jen -> finalize wireframes by Thu, Sam -> land trace schema PR in next sprint, Maria -> draft acceptance doc + test plan, Priyanka -> update roadmap & customer comms.
Alex: Thanks. If nobody objects I’ll mark this thread as the working pact. :thumbsup:
Maria: No objections. Marking as agreed from product side.
Sam: Sounds good.
Jen: Ack.
Priyanka: Ack.
Alex: Closing sync — follow ups in the tickets above.
